::: {#rem-cross-entropy-wrong-code}
#### Cross-entropy is the cost of the wrong code

Write $H_2(p)$ for the entropy of a random variable with mass function $p$,
and $D_2(p \,\|\, q)$ for the
[Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence)
of $q$ from $p$, both with base-2 logarithms.
Cross-entropy splits into those two parts:

$$H_2(p, q) = H_2(p) + D_2(p \,\|\, q).$$

By @thm-source-coding, no uniquely decodable code averages fewer than $H_2(p)$ bits.
By @thm-wrong-code, a code built for $q$
costs about $D_2(p \,\|\, q)$ bits per value more than that.
The divergence is never negative,
and it is $0$ only when $q = p$ [@cover2006elements, section 2.6],
so the excess vanishes only when the code was built for the true distribution.
@cover2006elements [section 5.4] state @thm-wrong-code
in this form, with $H_2(p) + D_2(p \,\|\, q)$ in place of $H_2(p, q)$.

:::
